comments.body:
ROOT CAUSE (established from the six REVIEW_RESULT sidecars on epic 0e68-41eb-5782-4336, before any code change).

Premise correction first — two parts of the hypothesis in the description are FALSE, and saying so matters because they would have pointed the fix at the wrong seam:

1. Scores are NOT carried. The blocking G6 enrichment finding (norm_id n9d22a867f4a4d027) scored validity 0.8 -> 1.0 -> 1.0 -> 0.8889 across the four rounds it appeared in. Pass-2 re-verified and Pass-3 recomputed it every round. The 0.8889 in the final round is 8/9 of the graded set (no_existing_mitigation="no", the rest "yes"); every other finding in that same round also landed on 0.8889, which is what made it LOOK like a carried constant.

2. The review was NOT reading stale material. material_parts["description"] changed on every round (ba10ac32/10135 -> 9aa1e506/7388 -> af4a3972/7927 -> caf24a66/7972 -> caf24a66 -> bb528569/7468), and attest.current_material_fingerprint("0e68-...") today returns 0e6136527d98385c, exactly the final sidecar's material_fingerprint. orchestrator.assemble_context(...).plan_text is 7568 chars and DOES contain the addressing text verbatim ("_build_snapshot (fetcher.py) iterates the configured project set for the base JQL fan-out AND its three enrichment passes -- get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map called once per project"). prompts.shared_plan_prefix() puts it in the Pass-2 verifier's context. So the verifier had the refuting provision in front of it and still answered claims_absence="yes" AND absence_confirmed_in_context="yes".

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM — a self-feeding recall ratchet, visible as an empty-evidence signature.

pass1.run_pass1 (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py, the "Recall" block after the ISF pass) injects each prior concern with a hardcoded `"evidence": []` and `"impact": ""`, keeping only finding/suggested_fix/criteria/location. Tracking norm_id n9d22a867f4a4d027 across the sidecars:

  round 2 (1786610680...): evidence has 3 items  -> FRESH finder output, block
  round 3 (1786611175...): evidence == []        -> recall injection, block
  round 4 (1786612154...): evidence == []        -> recall injection, block
  round 5 (1786612828...): evidence == []        -> recall injection, block
  round 6 (1786613356...): evidence == []        -> recall injection, block

The fresh finder stopped emitting it after round 2 — i.e. the finder DID register that the edited plan addressed it. Every subsequent emission is a verbatim replay. The same signature repeats on nc667728c37b59937 (6 -> 0 -> 0 -> 0), n9f9c21c542f8a621 (5 -> 0 -> 0), ndae84ec4f706d352 (4 -> 0 -> 0): the sidecar accumulates a growing ballast of zero-evidence replays.

Why it never terminates: sidecar.prior_concerns() selects prior findings on `decision in {"block","advisory"}` and `priority >= RECALL_MIN_PRIORITY` only. A recalled finding is re-verified, re-decided as `block`, and re-persisted by build_payload._slim — whose allow-list drops the `_recall` marker — so on the next run it is indistinguishable from a fresh finding and re-qualifies for recall. Recall was designed as a one-shot backstop for a flaky finder ("verdict-flips on IDENTICAL material are a RECALL problem" — sidecar.py:357) and instead became a permanent ratchet. Nothing on the path ever consults material_fingerprint, even though the sidecar records it.

Why Pass-2 does not act as the designed backstop ("A candidate the current plan resolved fails Pass-2 validity and is dropped — recall never blocks on memory alone", pass1.py): the injected candidate is an assertion with NO grounding. review_kernel/verify.finding_listing renders `evidence:` as an empty string, so evidence_entails_finding has nothing to test and the verifier confirms the bare claim. The absence veto in review_kernel/decide.py:660 (claims_absence=yes AND absence_confirmed_in_context=no) is exactly the right lever and never fires, because the verifier answers absence_confirmed_in_context="yes" on an evidence-less restatement rather than searching the plan for the refuting provision. v2 sidecars DO persist evidence losslessly (story 4e19) — prior_concerns simply never reads it.

FIX SHAPE (all three confined to the recall path; fresh-finding verification untouched):
(a) prior_concerns carries the persisted `evidence` (and `impact`) into the concern, and run_pass1 injects them, so Pass-2 re-grounds the claim's original quotes against the CURRENT plan instead of rubber-stamping a bare assertion;
(b) a prior finding with NO persisted grounding evidence is INELIGIBLE for recall — there is nothing to re-ground it with, and that set is exactly the previous recall injections, which breaks the ratchet (and works on the already-written sidecars, no migration);
(c) recall is suppressed wholesale when the prior sidecar's material_fingerprint differs from attest.current_material_fingerprint() — on CHANGED material the fresh finder's silence is evidence the edit resolved the finding, not a miss, which is recall's own stated contract.
Plus: persist `recalled` in build_payload._slim so the ratchet is visible offline, and record the suppression reason in coverage.

Related prior work checked, none touched: 1656 (completion_tool_policy per-kind claim) and 1700 (completion verifier store pinning) are on the completion-verifier path; the sidecar margin work is in decision_margin/_slim's scoring fields, not the eligibility filter.

comments.body:
LANDED + LIVE VALIDATION.

Merged to main as f2394af853 (Gerrit change 1722, LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, submitted and replicated). Worktree realigned.

Live validation on epic 0e68-41eb-5782-4336 (outrageous-uncultured-wildebeast), run against the fix:

- The target finding is GONE. norm_id n9d22a867f4a4d027 ("the multi-project inbound fetch child ... does not address the three per-project enrichment passes") was a `block` with `evidence: []` at priority 0.8889 in the immediately preceding round; with the fix in place it is absent from the finding set entirely. The ratchet is broken end-to-end in production, on the already-written sidecars, with no migration.
- Recall still works where it should. Three findings came back with `recalled: true` carrying 4, 6 and 5 evidence items — grounded priors re-surfaced and re-verified against the current plan, which is the behaviour recall was built for.
- The epic still BLOCKed at that point, on GENUINE findings rather than a replay: a G6 store-compat "no window" defect emitted FRESH with 3 evidence items, plus its independently corroborating recalled twin (4 evidence items), and three G3 advisories on parent AC2/AC7 coverage in child 1734. That is the intended shape — a real gap still blocks.

Honest limit: `coverage["recall_suppressed"]` is set in the Pass-1 coverage dict and unit-tested at the `prior_concerns` seam, but `build_payload` persists only a fixed subset of coverage keys, so the stamp is not visible in the sidecar (the existing `isf` key has the same gap). Widening what `build_payload` persists was out of scope.

Test suites at the landed sha: integration 194 passed / 1 skipped; unit 12739 passed / 52 skipped with one failure in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py::test_pass_summary_reports_the_decline_count — the known order-dependent hammerkop flake, which passes in isolation and is in a package this change does not touch.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

A plan-review finding, once surfaced, can replay verbatim on every later review of the same
ticket even after the plan is edited to fully address it, so the revise-review loop never
converges and each round costs a full LLM review. Confirmed on epic `0e68-41eb-5782-4336`,
where one G6 finding blocked five consecutive rounds. The root cause is recorded in full on
this ticket's first comment; the load-bearing evidence is summarised below.

## Approach

`sidecar.prior_concerns` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py`) selects prior findings for
re-surfacing on `decision in {"block","advisory"}` and `priority >= RECALL_MIN_PRIORITY`
alone. `pass1.run_pass1` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py`, the "Recall" block after the
ISF pass) then injects each one with a hardcoded `"evidence": []` and `"impact": ""`. Because
`sidecar.build_payload._slim` persists an explicit allow-list that does not include the
`_recall` marker, a re-surfaced finding is re-verified, re-decided `block`, and re-persisted
indistinguishably from a fresh one — so it re-qualifies for recall every round. Recall was
built as a one-shot backstop for a finder that MISSED a finding on identical material
(`sidecar.py`, the recall section comment) and instead behaves as a permanent ratchet.

The designed Pass-2 backstop does not fire because the injected candidate carries no
grounding: `review_kernel/verify.finding_listing` renders `evidence:` as an empty string, so
`evidence_entails_finding` has nothing to test, and the absence veto in
`review_kernel/decide.py` (`claims_absence == "yes"` AND `absence_confirmed_in_context ==
"no"`) never fires because the verifier confirms the bare restatement instead of searching the
current plan for the refuting provision. Verified on the epic's final sidecar: the blocking
finding recorded `claims_absence: "yes"`, `absence_confirmed_in_context: "yes"`, `evidence:
[]`, while `orchestrator.assemble_context(...).plan_text` (7568 chars, in the verifier's
context via `prompts.shared_plan_prefix`) contains the refuting provision verbatim.

The fix keeps all three changes inside the recall eligibility/injection path so fresh-finding
verification is untouched:

1. `prior_concerns` carries the prior finding's persisted `evidence` (and `impact`) into the
   concern, and `run_pass1` injects them instead of blanking them. v2 sidecars already persist
   `evidence` losslessly (`build_payload._slim`); `prior_concerns` simply never read it. This
   is the re-grounding: Pass-2 now judges the original quotes against the CURRENT plan text
   rather than rubber-stamping an assertion with nothing behind it.
2. A prior finding with no persisted grounding evidence is INELIGIBLE for recall — there is
   nothing to re-ground it with. That set is exactly the previous recall injections, so this
   breaks the ratchet, and it works against already-written sidecars with no migration.
3. Recall is suppressed wholesale when the prior sidecar's `material_fingerprint` differs from
   `attest.current_material_fingerprint(ticket_id, repo_root=...)`. On CHANGED material the
   fresh finder's silence is evidence the edit resolved the finding, not a miss — which is
   recall's own stated contract. Both fingerprints must be present for the comparison to
   apply; a missing one leaves recall enabled (best-effort, as today).

Why this shape rather than a new LLM re-grounding sub-call: the sidecars already record every
signal needed (`evidence`, `material_fingerprint`), so the gap closes deterministically at
zero additional token cost and stays unit-testable without a model. A genuinely unaddressed
gap still blocks, because the fresh Pass-1 finder re-emits it with real evidence on the
changed plan (observed on the epic: the finding was found fresh with 3 evidence items while it
was genuinely unaddressed, and only went evidence-empty once the plan was fixed).

`build_payload._slim` additionally persists a `recalled` boolean so the ratchet is visible in
offline calibration, and `run_pass1` records the suppression reason in `coverage`.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py` — `prior_concerns`: carry `evidence`/`impact`,
  exclude evidence-less priors, add the material-fingerprint suppression; `build_payload._slim`:
  persist `recalled`.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py` — the recall block: inject the carried
  `evidence`/`impact`; record the suppression/eligibility counts in `coverage`.
- `tests/unit/test_pass1_recall.py` — the regression test for the replay scenario, plus fixture
  updates for the tightened eligibility contract.

No change to `review_kernel/verify.py`, `review_kernel/decide.py`, the verifier prompts, or any
fresh-finding path. The completion-verifier work on tickets `1656` and `1700` is on a different
path (`completion_subcall.py` / `completion_sidecar.py`) and is not touched.

## Testing

- Happy path: a prior `block` finding WITH evidence, on UNCHANGED material, is still recalled
  and now carries its evidence and impact into the injected candidate.
- The replay regression: a prior `block` finding with `evidence: []` (the signature a previous
  recall injection leaves) is NOT recalled, so a second review cannot replay it.
- Changed material: a fully eligible prior finding is NOT recalled when the sidecar's
  `material_fingerprint` differs from the current one, and IS recalled when they match.
- Edge/degrade: a sidecar missing `material_fingerprint`, and an `attest` lookup that raises,
  both leave recall enabled rather than failing the review (the existing best-effort posture,
  covered by the existing `test_prior_concerns_best_effort_on_reader_error`).
- Unaffected: `test_finder_never_receives_prior_findings` and
  `test_recalled_candidate_dropped_by_pass2_when_resolved` continue to pass unchanged, pinning
  that Pass-1 independence and the Pass-2 validity backstop are not weakened.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The root cause is recorded as a comment on this ticket naming where recall reinjects
      findings and why plan-text re-grounding is skipped — checked by `rebar show
      deceitful-flannel-jerboa` showing the comment.
- [x] A prior finding with no persisted grounding evidence is not returned by
      `sidecar.prior_concerns` — checked by a new unit test in `tests/unit/test_pass1_recall.py`
      asserting the evidence-less concern is absent from the result while an
      evidence-carrying sibling is present.
- [x] Recall is suppressed when the prior sidecar's `material_fingerprint` differs from the
      current one and fires when they match — checked by a paired unit test that monkeypatches
      `attest.current_material_fingerprint`.
- [x] A recalled candidate reaches Pass-2 carrying the prior finding's `evidence` and `impact`
      — checked by a unit test asserting the `_recall`-marked finding returned by
      `pass1.run_pass1` has the non-empty evidence list from the concern.
- [x] Fresh-finding verification is unchanged — checked by
      `tests/unit/test_pass1_recall.py::test_finder_never_receives_prior_findings` and
      `::test_recalled_candidate_dropped_by_pass2_when_resolved` passing without edits.
- [x] The full local gate set is green — checked by `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and
      `pytest -m "not integration and not external"` plus `tests/integration` passing.
- [x] Live validation: `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1 rebar review-plan
      outrageous-uncultured-wildebeast` no longer emits the per-project enrichment finding
      against the current description — checked by reading the resulting verdict and reporting
      it on this ticket.

## Implementation note

Landed as `f2394af853`. `coverage["recall_suppressed"]` is set in the Pass-1 coverage dict and
unit-tested at the `prior_concerns` seam, but `build_payload` persists only a fixed subset of
coverage keys, so it does not reach the sidecar (as is already true of `isf`). Out of scope here.
